content.title: Why HR Departments Often Don’t Live Up to Employees’ Expectations
content.summary: On one hand, HR departments are frequently tasked with recruiting and hiring the best people possible and, ideally, helping these individuals succeed at, and be fulfilled by, their jobs.  To look at what HR departments do—and don’t do—well, we spoke with Allison Elias, assistant professor of business administration at the Darden School of Business at the University of Virginia and author of “The Rise of Corporate Feminism,” which looks at the development of human resource management in the latter half of the 20th century.  ALLISON ELIAS: The HR we know today—with credentialed professionals managing tasks like hiring and firing, benefits, training, grievances—didn’t really come along until the 1980s.
